sentences.text:
Ms. Sakshee P. Chavan,
Advocate for the Respondents.
Coram : A.S. Chandurkar & Jitendra Jain, Jj Date : 16Th April, 2024.

It is submitted by the learned counsel for the petitioner that clause 11 of the Airport Entry Permit Guidelines, 2022 ought to be read in its entirety for the reason that clause 11.9 refers to a situation where the applicant is convicted while clause 11.9.1 makes reference to serious crimes that have been described therein.

Under clause 11.10, if First Information Report is registered and/or a case is pending before the Court for serious categories of crimes referred to in clause 11.9.1, the decision of the Director General, Bureau of Civil Aviation Security is treated to be final.
2. It is submitted that in the present case, a First Information Report has been lodged against the petitioner under Sections 313 and 376(2)(n) 3-WP(L)-12377-2024.doc Dixit of Indian Penal Code.
These offences do not qualify as serious crimes under clause 11.9.1.
This aspect has not been considered by the Appellate Authority.
3. Issue notice to the respondents, returnable on 7th May 2024.
Ms. Sakshee Chavan, learned counsel waives notice for the respondents.
4. Affidavit-in-reply shall be filed prior to the returnable date.
